questions.question: Look at the graph. Which fruit is most?
questions.explain: Count the pictures for each fruit. Apples has the most pictures. The trap is picking the one with the fewest.

questions.question: Which toy is fewest?
questions.explain: Count the pictures for each toy. Dolls has the fewest pictures. Be careful not to pick the one with the most.

questions.question: How many more apples than oranges?
questions.explain: Take the smaller number away from the bigger one: 9 minus 6 is 3. The trap is saying 9 or adding them to get 15.

questions.question: How many more balls than dolls?
questions.explain: Take 3 away from 8 to get 5 more. The trap is saying 8 or adding to make 11.

questions.question: Maya has 8 star stickers and 5 heart stickers. How many more star stickers than heart stickers?
questions.explain: Take 5 away from 8 to get 3 more. The trap is saying 8 or adding to make 13.

questions.question: Sam found rocks, shells, and stars at the beach. Which is most?
questions.explain: Count each group. Shells has 9, which is the most. The trap is picking stars, which has the fewest.

visual.caption: Things Sam found at the beach

questions.question: At the farm there are 10 ducks and 4 pigs. How many more ducks than pigs?
questions.explain: Take 4 away from 10 to get 6 more ducks. The trap is saying 10 or adding to make 14.

questions.question: Ana counted 5 apples and 3 pears. She wants to say how many more apples than pears. What is the right way?
questions.explain: To find how many more, take the smaller number away from the bigger one. Adding gives the total, not the difference.

questions.question: Ben has 3 red cars and 7 blue cars. He gives away 2 blue cars. How many more blue cars than red cars now?
questions.explain: Take 2 away from 7 to get 5 blue cars, then take 3 away from 5 to get 2 more. The trap is stopping at 5.

questions.question: Mia says: 'There are 9 flowers and 6 bugs. There are 9 more flowers than bugs.' What went wrong?
questions.explain: Mia said 9, but 9 minus 6 is only 3 more. She should have taken the smaller number away, not just said the bigger one.

questions.question: At the picnic, 7 kids brought apples and 4 kids brought pears. Then 1 more kid brought an apple. How many more kids brought apples than pears now?
questions.explain: Add 1 to 7 to get 8 apple kids, then take 4 away from 8 to get 4 more. The trap is stopping at 8.

questions.question: Look at the graph. Which sentence is true?
options: There are 9 more birds than cats.
Squirrels are the most on the graph.
There are 2 more birds than cats.
questions.explain: Count the rows: birds 9, cats 7, so 9 take away 7 is 2 more birds. Saying 9 just gives the bigger number, not how many more.

visual.caption: Animals we saw on the school walk

questions.question: Leo looks at the graph. He says geese are the most. What went wrong?
options: He picked the fewest row, not the most.
He added the rows instead of comparing.
Nothing is wrong, geese have a short row.
He named a bird when a number was needed.
questions.explain: The most is the longest row, so crows are the most. The shortest row, geese, means fewest — that is the easy mix-up here.
